chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: If you wear a garment in your Ihram that is not permissible for you to wear, then recite the Talbiyah and repeat your Ghusl. And if you wear a shirt, then tear it and remove it from beneath your feet.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for wearing a stitched garment during Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for wearing stitched garments during Ihram, distinguishing between general prohibited clothing requiring a ritual bath and a shirt that must be torn and removed from beneath the feet. It reflects the Ja'fari jurisprudence view that the violation is rectified through purification and the physical removal of the garment, ensuring the pilgrim's state of consecration remains valid.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If you were to wear clothes inside your Ihraam, which is not correct for you to wear, so you exclaim Talbiyya, and repeat your washing. And, if you were to wear a shirt, so tear it, and take it out from beneath your feet’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you wear in the state of Ihram a cloth which is not proper, you must say Talbiyah again and take Ghusl (bath); and if you wear a shirt, then tear it and remove it from the direction of the bottom of your feet.’”
